doc: The typical call at 64x32 with every input float64 (the arithmetic of a float64 port): the only difference between two correct implementations is the summation order of the row mean, which flips a decision only within an ulp of the target, so the result is reproduced to a few final-bracket widths (atol 1e-9 = 3.5 x 2.9e-10). Arguments: s, fine, target, streak, subtexel and offset are the inputs of that name when listed; an unlisted streak or offset (default 0.0) is the scalar in params, an unlisted subtexel is None; prm holds the GenParams fields compose reads. The 36 steps and the bracket [-10, 10] are literals of the source. Measured: one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 0 (worst of 6 random trials); no difference was observed at all.
